extracted.intended_audience: academic journal editors (Taylor & Francis and similar publishers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for journal editors on conducting and documenting rigorous, unbiased peer review for original research manuscripts, with emphasis on using at least two independent reviewers and maintaining transparent records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum of two independent peer reviewers for original research
rubrics_metrics.description: All Taylor & Francis original research publications must undergo rigorous peer review including ... Anonymous refereeing by a minimum of two independent expert referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key to best practice is to make sure peer review reports are sourced from at least two independent referees for every original research article we publish. This reduces bias and the chance that errors/flaws are missed, and helps support editorial decisions if challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an independent peer reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent peer reviewer is an expert in the field the research article describes, or the specific techniques, methods, or study design underlying it. They have no obvious competing interest that may bias their opinion of the work under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main indicators of a competing interest include recent or regular co-authorship with any of the manuscript authors and affiliation with the same institute as the authors. Note other less-detectable interests (personal, political, religious) may exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid selecting reviewers from same institution or department
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid the possibility of bias compromising the decision-making process, it is important to get reports from two independent peer reviewers and you should not select two reviewers from the same institution or department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, independent reviewers should not be from the same institution or department as the handling editor. Doing so risks reducing independence of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling editor must not act as independent peer reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript’s handling editor should not act as an independent peer reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A handling editor may be the associate editor who has organised peer review; if they also review the manuscript it can lead to accusations of bias, narrowing of scope, and risk that the paper hasn't been fully and fairly assessed. In double-anonymous journals, the handling editor would know author identities and so must not act as reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-in-chief should not review papers they handle
rubrics_metrics.description: An editor-in-chief with responsibility for the final outcome of a paper should not act as a peer reviewer on a paper they are handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids conflicts where the decision-maker is also providing review input that could influence the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board members may act as reviewers if independent and not handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An Editorial Board Member may be considered an independent peer reviewer if they meet the independence criteria and are not involved in the direct handling or decision making for that particular paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their involvement must comply with the expected process outlined in the journal's Instructions for Authors/IFAs and local editorial policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial screening prior to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All Taylor & Francis original research publications must undergo rigorous peer review including: Initial screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may desk reject at this stage without peer review if the submission fails to meet journal standards of quality or novelty, or if the research is out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor assessment informed by reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor assessment of the work’s readiness for publication, informed by two or more independent referees’ comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final decision is the editor’s responsibility; taking into account a range of expert assessments supports making a fair editorial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a peer review system to record activity
rubrics_metrics.description: If your journal has a peer review system in place, all peer review activity should be conducted in the system to maintain and record an unbiased and appropriate peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conducting peer review within the system ensures records are available for audit and helps defend editorial handling if challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual peer review records if no system; must comply with data protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals not on a peer review system must make sure that manual peer review records are created and securely retained in a format compliant with global data protection legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligent record keeping enables publisher support if there is any need to audit peer review quality or defend manuscript handling in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory two reviewers for clinical / human / animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical manuscripts and articles describing research involving humans or animals must always have at least two independent reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is non-optional due to ethical and safety implications of such research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reviewers required for controversial or divisive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: If an article is on a controversial or divisive topic, advice from multiple reviewers is also required, regardless of manuscript length or type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures more balanced assessment where topics are contentious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and ability to substantiate editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: As an editor you must be transparent in how you handle manuscripts and be able to substantiate the editorial decisions you make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating peer review best practice has been followed reinforces confidence that published work is properly validated and reliably adds to the academic record; it also helps defend decisions in appeals or integrity challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage diversity of reviewer voices and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Securing reports from two or more independent peer reviewers helps make sure a range of voices are presented and promotes fair and full evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One individual may not assess all elements; attracting a diversity of voices balances different biases and improves editors' ability to make balanced and fair decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and develop a healthy reviewer pool; mentor reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing a healthy reviewer pool and mentoring others to become expert reviewers is a key element of the editor role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available resources (editors guide, training modules, videos) to find and work with reviewers and to support reviewer development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation path when editor is sole expert
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter a paper that is so specific only you have sufficient knowledge to handle it, you should escalate this to your Editorial Contact, who’ll be able to recommend options for additional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not act as reviewer yourself; seek additional expert support to ensure fair assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors may desk reject submissions without peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, editors may elect to desk reject a submission without peer review if it fails to meet journal standards of quality or novelty, or if the research described is out of scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desk rejection should be used where warranted, but decisions should be defensible and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping supports defense of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A robust peer review process and records support defense of editorial decisions, professional reputation, and the journal should an integrity challenge arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having two independent peer reviews demonstrates the paper was handled appropriately and in line with policy when appeals or complaints occur.
